title: Locally closed subset
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space (for instance the underlying space of a scheme). A subset $E\subseteq X$ is *locally closed* if there are an open subset $U\subseteq X$ and a closed subset $Z\subseteq X$ with $E=U\cap Z$; equivalently, $E$ is open in its closure $\overline E$.

source.place: Stacks Project, Topology, Section 'Basic notions' (Tag 004E), item 'locally closed subset' (listed there without definition; the definition $E=U\cap Z$ is the standard one and the equivalence with 'open in its closure' is elementary: take $Z=\overline E$)
